title: Demand Service Rate Programs: The Starting Ceiling a Review Works From
content:
| The charges that fell due in the window | The starting ceiling |
|---|---|
| above half the tier's published credit limit but not above it | that invoiced total rounded up to the next whole multiple of 1000 US dollars |
| at or below half the tier's published credit limit | half that published credit limit |
| above the tier's published credit limit | neither term above displaces the published credit limit |

The published credit limit each row is measured against, by program under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Published credit limit (USD) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 7500 |
| Priority Response Program | 15000 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 25000 |
| Emergency Response Program | 40000 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 75000 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 150000 |

**Both sides of the halves (hypothetical).** On the Block Hour Service Program, whose published credit
limit is 25000 US dollars, half of that limit is 12500 US dollars. Charges of 12500 US dollars falling
due in the window give a starting ceiling of 12500 US dollars, that total standing at half the limit
rather than above it. Charges of 12600 US dollars give a starting ceiling of 13000 US dollars, being
that total rounded up to the next whole multiple of 1000 US dollars. Charges of 25000 US dollars give a
starting ceiling of 25000 US dollars, that total standing at the limit rather than above it and rounding
up to a whole multiple of 1000 US dollars leaving it where it is.
